incentives.name: Data Center Investment Program
incentives.what: Exemptions from a range of state and local taxes (including sales/use tax on equipment) for data centers investing at least $250M over 60 months and creating 20+ full-time jobs paying at least 120% of county median wage; must be carbon neutral or green-building certified. 20-year benefit issued as renewable 5-year certificates; 20% construction-wage credit in underserved areas. DCEO stops processing applications as of July 1, 2026 per a June 5, 2026 governor's directive.
incentives.value_known: An estimated $666.6 million in data center tax credits committed since 2019 (Capitol News Illinois).

laws_and_bills.name: POWER Act (Protecting Our Water and Energy Resources Act), HB 5513
laws_and_bills.what: Energy and water use rules for new data centers. Not passed in the spring 2026 session; could return in the fall veto session.

laws_and_bills.name: SB 1050 (Sen. Darby Hills)
laws_and_bills.what: Would bar data centers within 3 miles of another municipality's boundary without that municipality's written consent and add public notice rules. Not passed in spring 2026.

local_rules.what: Mayor Brandon Johnson signed an executive order creating new data center review steps and a task force, and asked City Council to consider a temporary citywide moratorium while rules are drafted.
local_rules.status: executive order in effect; moratorium proposed

local_rules.what: County Board passed a 12-month data center moratorium 6-4 on May 19, 2026; the State's Attorney said June 18 it was not legally binding because procedures were not followed. A zoning ordinance failed 5-6.
After rejecting Project Kilo, the village board approved a temporary moratorium on new data center proposals while it writes rules.
Updated CyrusOne CHI-11 agreement caps water use at 40,000 gallons/day and adds sound-testing rules.

dockets.what: ComEd changes to new service requests from large demand project applicants or customers (data centers) and Rider DSE. Approved March 2026: security deposits start at $1M for 50-200 MW and rise $500,000 per extra 100 MW; a letter of credit is needed above $2M. The order told staff to open a follow-up investigation by April 23, 2026 into further ratepayer protections (that docket number not found). Docket numbers per NRG direct testimony: https://stg1-www.nrg.com/content/dam/nrg/web/en/multimedia/documents/energy-policy/nrg-ex-1.0-direct-testimony-of-james-r-dauphinais-icc-docket-nos-25-0677-0679-comed-large-load-tariff-case.pdf
